extracted.intended_audience: national securities exchanges, ETF sponsors, fund counsel, and SEC staff evaluating or preparing a rule filing to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares (Spot Bitcoin ETPs)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluation criteria used by an exchange and the SEC for listing and trading a Spot Bitcoin exchange-traded product structured as Commodity-Based Trust Shares, including surveillance, custody, pricing, and investor-protection requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule change must be consistent with the requirements of section 6(b)(5) of the Act, specifically that (i) a national securities exchange's rules are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices; and (ii) the exchange proposal is designed, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange must demonstrate how the proposal meets both prongs. The filing should explain why the proposal prevents fraud/manipulation and how it serves investor protection/public interest (e.g., by offering a regulated, transparent vehicle versus riskier alternatives). If the Commission disagrees on fraud/manipulation mitigation, investor-protection considerations may nevertheless weigh in favor of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance-sharing agreement requirement for Commodity-Based Trust Shares
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet the 'prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices' standard for Commodity-Based Trust Shares, the listing exchange must demonstrate that there is a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement in place with a regulated market of significant size related to the underlying commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, the Commission has required such an agreement (often satisfied by joint ISG membership) because it provides necessary information to detect, investigate, and deter manipulation. The filing should identify the regulated market of significant size and the surveillance-sharing arrangement or else explain alternative means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hallmarks of a surveillance-sharing agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A surveillance-sharing agreement is characterized by: (i) sharing information about market trading activity, clearing activity, and customer identity; (ii) reasonable ability of parties to obtain access to and produce requested information; and (iii) absence of rules, laws, or practices that would impede one party from obtaining or producing such information to the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the scope of information exchange, the legal ability to obtain/produce information, and any limitations. The Commission has treated joint membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group (ISG) as meeting these hallmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and test for a 'regulated market of significant size'
rubrics_metrics.description: A market (or group of markets) is a market of significant size if: (a) there is a reasonable likelihood that a person attempting to manipulate the ETP would also have to trade on that market to manipulate the ETP (so that surveillance-sharing would help detect/deter misconduct); and (b) it is unlikely that trading in the ETP would be the predominant influence on prices in that market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange should present empirical evidence (e.g., trading volumes, open interest, market capitalization) and analysis showing (a) the linkage such that manipulators would need to trade in the regulated market, and (b) that the ETP would not dominate price formation in that market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable alternative: 'other means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices'
rubrics_metrics.description: If a surveillance-sharing agreement with a regulated market of significant size is not available, a listing exchange may instead demonstrate that other means to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices are sufficient to satisfy section 6(b)(5) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence and argument for other mitigation measures (e.g., geographic diversity and fragmentation of spot trading, role of arbitrageurs, use of reputable custodians, transparent reference rates, exchange surveillance capabilities). The Exchange must carry the burden of proof to show these other means are adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating manipulation linkage via derivatives market surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the spot market is largely unregulated, reliance on a regulated derivatives market (e.g., CME Bitcoin Futures) can satisfy the 'regulated market of significant size' requirement if that derivatives market's surveillance captures effects from spot market manipulation and price discovery is led by the derivatives market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing should explain the surveillance capabilities of the derivatives market, empirical evidence that futures lead price formation (citations, studies), and how surveillance-sharing with the derivatives market would assist in detecting manipulative conduct affecting the ETP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating that ETP trading would not predominate price influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange must show that trading in the proposed ETP would not be the predominant force influencing prices in the referenced regulated market or the spot market (factors include daily trading volume, market capitalization, liquidity, and open interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide market metrics (e.g., daily notional volume, open interest, number of large holders) and qualitative discussion explaining why the ETP's trading would not overwhelm price formation in underlying markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a transparent, reliable Reference Rate / NAV inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund's Reference Rate (e.g., the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate—New York Variant) and NAV calculation methodology must be transparent, replicable, and derived from credible constituent spot venues; any permanent change to NAV calculation requires a proposed rule change under Rule 19b-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the reference rate's composition, calculation window, constituent platforms, and transparency features. Explain how BZX Official Closing Price and NAV are determined and disclosed. Highlight that calculation rules aim for maximum transparency and real-time replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody and service-provider standards to protect investors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund should use qualified, regulated custodians for bitcoin and cash (e.g., Coinbase Custody Trust Company and Bank of New York Mellon) and appropriate custody practices (including cold storage) to mitigate risks like counterparty insolvency, cyber attacks, and theft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail custody arrangements, segregation of assets, cold storage procedures, custody audits, insurance (if any), and oversight of service providers. Explain why using regulated custodians and professional service providers affords protections relative to direct holding or OTC vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor-protection rationale favoring Spot Bitcoin ETPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Approve proposals based on investor-protection benefits of a regulated, exchange-listed Spot Bitcoin ETP versus alternatives (direct spot holdings, OTC funds, or futures-only ETFs), including reduced counterparty risk, periodic reporting, and transparent trading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how registration and reporting under the 1933 Act and Exchange Act, custody by qualified custodians, and exchange oversight reduce risks faced by retail investors compared to offshore or OTC options. Quantify harms where possible (e.g., losses tied up in bankruptcies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Bitcoin Futures ETF drawbacks for long-term investors
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing product structures, consider that Bitcoin Futures ETFs can incur roll costs (leading to performance lag versus spot), may hit position limits, and could be forced to hold non-futures assets—all of which alter investor economics and risk profiles relative to Spot Bitcoin ETPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analysis comparing expected long-term costs and tracking differences between futures-based products and spot-backed products, and explain how such factors weigh in the investor-protection analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical market metrics to support claims (volume, open interest, holder concentration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete market data—daily notional trading volume on futures exchanges, open interest, number of large open interest holders, and spot market liquidity—to support arguments about market significance, price discovery, and manipulability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant time windows and figures (e.g., CME Bitcoin Futures daily notional volume, open interest levels) and explain how these metrics satisfy the 'market of significant size' tests or other standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of regulatory and industry developments in evaluating proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider changes in the regulatory landscape (e.g., custody rule proposals, no-action letters, BitLicense grants, enforcement actions) and the maturation of regulated service providers when assessing whether investor protections have materially improved since earlier filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document relevant regulatory milestones, emergence of regulated custodians, and industry adoption (institutional investors, asset managers) to show changed circumstances that bear on the Commission's review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on precedent and judicial findings in standard application
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Commission precedent (e.g., Teucrium Approval, Winklevoss Order, prior Commodity-Based Trust approvals) and relevant court decisions (e.g., Grayscale v. SEC) as part of the analytical framework for whether a proposal satisfies the required standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain similarities or distinctions from precedent, and use judicial findings (e.g., court commentary on inconsistency between futures approvals and spot disapprovals) to support claims that the current proposal should be approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and disclosure controls (market hours, closing price definitions, cash equivalents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify operational definitions and controls that affect trading and valuation, such as Regular Trading Hours, BZX Official Closing Price definition, permitted cash equivalents (short-term instruments <3 months), and operational limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide definitions consistent with Exchange rules (e.g., Rule 11.23(a)(3) for BZX Official Closing Price), describe permissible cash-equivalent instruments, and disclose operational processes for NAV calculation, creation/redemption, and trading.
